card.title: PROOF: logs land for every kind of run including the dead ones and the repair run, planted secrets never survive, a plan run's kept log names its step and carries that step's effort, and the first weekly report is produced

thread.body:
🧭 routing-verdict: **OPERATOR** — Not code — a deploy, a migration run, a secret.

**Why:** the epic's proof card, routed by the proof-and-demo check off the card itself: the card carries an explicit role label, which says where it goes — no judgement, and no model asked An epic is confirmed by something other than its builder, so the fleet is never sent at this card.

**Where it goes:** Todo. **Who handles it there:** operator.
**Marked:** `hand-built`, `no-code` — so the sweep neither dispatches a run nor reports the card as stalled.
This card is **not** dispatched to the fleet: the promoter reads this verdict and leaves it where a person will find it.

**Proof by system** — waits on DRE-4271, DRE-5350, DRE-5353, DRE-5356 and the Agent-Bureau fleet pause (the run it observes is switched off until Stage 1 lands); closes itself on evidence, never reaches the CEO.

_Sorted 2026-10-02 17:24 PT under the CEO's rule of 2026-10-02: a proof runs in the sandboxes and is closed on evidence. Only a fact he alone can see goes to him._

🧳 hand-built-migration: label removed (`hand-built`).

**What it read:** `hand-built` was put on this card automatically — applied by Agent-Bureau (history entry) — and the card is a proof in Backlog.

**The rule it followed:** a proof keeps `no-code` and its lane; the proof dispatch takes it from Hand-work, and nothing about it needs the CEO's mark.

The CEO's rule of 2026-10-07: "Build it and let everyone know when i say built it, I'm saying this is a hand built card." The mark is his alone, so the one-time hand-built migration takes off every one the pipeline applied.
🧹 Reconcile: the 'Backlog' lane is being retired (DRE-4125) and nothing writes to it any more — moved to 'Queued', which is where the work now continues.

- **7 met:** 6,551 of 7,743 fingerprint rows since 10-02 carry effort. The rows match the objects both ways: 39066771344 has effort high on both, and 38999022487 has neither.
- **Releases:** AgentLogStack deploy carrying DRE-5032 and DRE-5351 was 10-01 17:02 PT. The first console release carrying DRE-4387 and DRE-5354 was v1.6.224, 10-01 17:10 PT.

Observation 8 filled on draft PR #3876 (commit 5b4a4e635) from DRE-5407's record of Sunday 2026-10-18: production filed DRE-7512 itself at 05:43:29 PT, alone in Green Light, with `Cost: $2.72 · 8 model calls` matching its row. record.text:
# Agent working logs, second pass — DRE-5357, observed in production on 2026-10-17

**Six of the eight observations are met. Two wait on one event each: observation 4 (the planted secret) waits on a sandbox build at night, and observation 6's `foundry` line waits on DRE-8154 shipping and an AgentLogStack deploy.** Observations 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 were read by hand against production on 2026-10-17. Observation 8 is cited from DRE-5407's merged record. This file was assembled on 2026-10-29 at about 4:40 PM PT from the draft on this branch, with observations 6 and 8 brought up to date (each says what changed and when).

**Why this is its own file.** The card asked for a dated second-pass section appended to `architecture/proofs/agent-working-logs.md`. The proof gate reads exactly one `.md` file that a record pull request ADDS under `docs/` or `architecture/`, so a section added to the existing file left the gate with no record to read (the `🧱 proof-record-stuck` notes on DRE-5357 from 10-21 on). The second pass therefore lives here, and `architecture/proofs/agent-working-logs.md` on `main` is left exactly as written.

Everything under "Observation 1" to "Observation 7" was read by hand by the operator session between **13:30 and 13:45 PT on 2026-10-17**. Nothing was written to any live system: no S3 put, no workflow dispatch, no re-run, no deploy, and the database reads ran in a `READ ONLY` transaction (`make db-read`). Times are Pacific.

**The first pass is `architecture/proofs/agent-working-logs.md` on `main`.** It is DRE-4272's record of 2026-09-20 and its two observation comments of that day: [13:02 PT](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-4272/superseded-re-filed-as-dre-5355-so-the-proof-card-is-the-epics-last#comment-3e10aabf) ("where this stands after a day") and [13:33 PT](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-4272/superseded-re-filed-as-dre-5355-so-the-proof-card-is-the-epics-last#comment-7414401d) (the turn-cap death cannot be arranged). It is left as written. The first pass numbers its observations differently: its 3 is this card's 4 (secrets), its 4 is 5 (public surfaces), its 5 is 6 (gaps) and its 6 is 8 (the report). This card's 3 (plan step and effort) and 7 (effort on the fingerprint) are new.

## Criteria

| Criterion | Result |
| --- | --- |
| All eight observations are recorded by hand, by the operator, in agent-bureau's `architecture/proofs/agent-working-logs.md`, each with its time (PT) and the command, taken against the live store, the live Record and the live board. | Not observed. waiting for a sandbox build on agent-bureau-demo that plants DRE-7513's throwaway probe secret, run 11 PM–3 AM PT (observation 4), and for DRE-8154 shipped and AgentLogStack deployed (observation 6's `foundry` line): observations 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 are recorded below with their PT times and commands, read on 2026-10-17 between 13:30 and 13:45 PT against the live store, the live Record and the live board, and observation 8 is cited from DRE-5407's merged record. Observation 4's scrub-by-value plant has not run, and `foundry`'s first agent run (40436818679, 2026-10-26 9:44 PM PT) was refused at upload. The second pass is in this file rather than in `architecture/proofs/agent-working-logs.md`, for the reason given above. |
| The record cites [DRE-4272](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-4272/superseded-re-filed-as-dre-5355-so-the-proof-card-is-the-epics-last)'s two 2026-09-20 observation comments, and the first-pass sections already in `architecture/proofs/agent-working-logs.md` on `main`, as its first pass, leaves those sections as written, and states per observation what changed since. | Met. The two DRE-4272 comments (13:02 and 13:33 PT, 2026-09-20) are linked above, and `architecture/proofs/agent-working-logs.md` on `main` is named as the first pass. This pull request leaves that file byte for byte as it is on `main`. The table under "Per observation" says what changed since the first pass, row by row. |
| Every sibling card in this epic is merged, and one AgentLogStack deploy taken after both [DRE-5032](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-5032/agent-bureau-porticos-agent-logs-are-refused-at-upload-its-oidc-tokens) and [DRE-5351](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-5351/agent-bureau-the-agent-log-upload-roles-trust-bureau-pipelines-red) merged has been applied, before the observations are taken; the record names that deploy's time. | Met. All 27 cards on the card's **Blocked by:** line read `Done` (`scripts/linear-api.py get DRE-<n>`, 2026-10-29 about 4:35 PM PT). DRE-5032 merged 2026-10-01 14:32 PT (#3005) and DRE-5351 at 14:54 PT (#3007). The AgentLogStack deploy carrying both finished `UPDATE_COMPLETE` at **2026-10-01 17:02:36 PT**, 16 days before the observations; see "The deploy and the release". |
| A console release carrying both [DRE-4387](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-4387/a-run-the-record-saw-whose-working-log-never-arrived-is-a-recorded-gap)'s and [DRE-5354](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-5354/agent-bureau-the-fingerprint-sweep-fills-each-runs-effort-from-the)'s merges is live, confirmed by commit ancestry against its tag, and each sweep has completed a pass on it, before observations 6 and 7 are read; the record names the release version and the time it went live. | Met. The first release carrying both merges is `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.224`, tagged 2026-10-01 17:10 PT. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` holds for `642733d4` (DRE-4387) and `49fb60f8` (DRE-5354) against `v1.6.491`, the version the console last reported (12:12 PT 2026-10-17), and `v1.6.492` (tagged 12:04 PT). The gap sweep completed a pass at 13:34:35 PT and the fingerprint sweep at 13:39:33 PT on 2026-10-17, before observations 6 and 7 were read. |
| Observation 2 cites a real run id for each kind that happened in the stated window, and says so plainly for any kind that did not; observation 3 does the same for a plan run that died in a later model step. | Met. The window is 2026-10-01 17:02 PT to 2026-10-17. Turn cap: agent-bureau `38314378287` attempt 1. 429: agent-bureau `37714053603`. Timeout: bureau-pipeline `38170959772`. A build-run turn-cap death did not happen in the window, and observation 2 says so. Observation 3's plan run that died in a later model step is bureau-pipeline `38329761597` (died in `oorevise`). |
| The CEO closes this card after reading the record. | Open: the CEO's step. |

## Per observation

| # | observation | verdict | what changed since the first pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | every run type lands a log | **met**, all seven kinds | `repair` joined: 40 logs since 2026-10-07 |
| 2 | the runs that died land too | **met**: turn cap, 429 and timeout each cited | was half proven, because no death had left a transcript |
| 3 | a plan run's kept log is the last model step's, carrying that step's effort | **met** | new |
| 4 | planted fake secrets never survive | **waiting**: for a sandbox build on agent-bureau-demo with `BUREAU_PLANT_PROBE` set, 11 PM–3 AM PT | the by-shape pass has now fired on 3 shapes; by value, still never. DRE-7513 (the throwaway probe secret) is now shipped |
| 5 | nothing reached a public surface | **met** | the secret-name listing (DRE-4391) is gone from the public log |
| 6 | every repo has a log, portico included, and a missing log shows as a gap | **met for six repos; `foundry` waiting** for DRE-8154 shipped and AgentLogStack deployed | portico now uploads; the gap sweep runs; `foundry` has a role, but it refuses foundry's sign-in form |
| 7 | a log carrying `effort` has a fingerprint row with that effort | **met** | new |
| 8 | the first weekly report is one card in Green Light, with its cost | **met**, cited from DRE-5407's merged record | production filed DRE-7512 itself, alone in Green Light, `$2.72 · 8 model calls` |

## The deploy and the release these observations were read on

**AgentLogStack: the deploy carrying both trust changes finished at 2026-10-01 17:02:36 PT.** DRE-5032 merged at 14:32 PT that day (agent-bureau #3005) and DRE-5351 at 14:54 PT (#3007). The stack's `UPDATE_COMPLETE` at 17:02:36 PT is the first one after both, and all six upload roles were updated in it, between 17:02:26 and 17:02:28 PT (`aws cloudformation describe-stack-events --stack-name AgentLogStack`). The live roles hold both changes, read with `aws iam get-role --role-name bureau-agent-log-upload-<slug>` at about 13:32 PT:

- **DRE-5032:** `bureau-agent-log-upload-portico`'s `:sub` condition accepts two patterns, `repo:dreadnought-foundry/portico:*` and the immutable `repo:dreadnought-foundry@226758887/portico@1299587579:*`.
- **DRE-5351:** every role's `job_workflow_ref` list holds seven workflows, including `dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/red-main-repair.yml@*`.

The stack has been updated 14 times since, most recently at 2026-10-16 14:49 PT. None of those updates changed an upload role; the last role update is still 2026-10-01 17:02 PT.

**The console: every release since v1.6.224 carries both sweeps.** DRE-4387's merge `642733d4` (#3006, 2026-10-01 14:27 PT) is first in `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.223`, and DRE-5354's merge `49fb60f8` (#3011, 15:19 PT) is first in **`agent-bureau-console-v1.6.224`, tagged 2026-10-01 17:10 PT** (`git tag --contains <sha>`). `git merge-base --is-ancestor` holds for both merges against `v1.6.491` and `v1.6.492`. The console's own heartbeat last named its version as `agent-bureau-console-v1.6.491`, at its shutdown at 12:12 PT on 2026-10-17. That followed the App Runner `UPDATE_SERVICE` of 12:01–12:04 PT, and `v1.6.492` was tagged at 12:04 PT. Either way, the running release carries both.

**Both sweeps completed passes on that release, read from the App Runner application log at about 13:41 PT** (`aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/apprunner/bureau-console-backend/…/application`):

- **Gap sweep, 13:34:35 PT:** `considered=5532 covered=2930 missing=2602 unchecked=0 recorded=0 failed=0`.
- **Fingerprint sweep, 13:39:33 PT:** `listed=12510 … read=5 inserted=5 refused=0 failed=0 … coverage=complete`.

---

## Observation 1 — every run type lands a log

**Met. All seven job kinds have stored logs, `repair` included, from six of the seven repos.** Listing taken at **13:30:05 PT**:

```
AWS_PROFILE=dreadnought aws s3 ls s3://agentlogstack-agentlogbucketffd20d5f-3yaboku3ceyv/agent-logs/ --recursive --region us-west-2
```

There were **10,022 working logs**: 1,961 from September and 8,061 from October. There were also 2,457 objects under a per-repo `github-calls/` prefix: DRE-6915's GitHub-call readings, which are not transcripts and are left out of every count here. Since 2026-10-02, the first day after the deploy:

| repo | diagnose | execute | fix | plan | repair | review | verify |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `agent-bureau` | 367 | 553 | 637 | 600 | 22 | 1,608 | 615 |
| `bureau-pipeline` | 200 | 408 | 446 | 408 | 18 | 1,018 | 0 |
| `portico` | 26 | 105 | 121 | 129 | 0 | 295 | 0 |
| `agent-bureau-demo` | 5 | 5 | 8 | 38 | 0 | 29 | 11 |
| `deltasolv` | 7 | 4 | 4 | 6 | 0 | 23 | 0 |
| `atlas` | 0 | 3 | 3 | 8 | 0 | 14 | 0 |

One stored key per kind, the newest of each at the listing, with the times as `s3 ls` printed them in PT:

| job | key | stored |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `execute` | `agent-logs/agent-bureau/2026-10-17/39066585218-1-execute.json.gz` | 10-17 13:29:32 |
| `review` | `agent-logs/agent-bureau/2026-10-17/39066771344-1-review.json.gz` | 10-17 13:28:48 |

**`repair` is the change.** The first repair log is `agent-logs/bureau-pipeline/2026-10-07/37645204926-1-repair.json.gz`, stored 2026-10-07 08:38 PT, three days after DRE-5353 merged (bureau-pipeline #711, 2026-10-04 08:57 PT). There are 40 since: 22 from agent-bureau and 18 from bureau-pipeline.

Zeros in the table are runs that did not happen, not refusals. bureau-pipeline, portico, atlas and deltasolv have no `verify` workflow, and only agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline have had a repair run that reached its model step. That second point is read from the gap spans, observation 6.

---

## Observation 2 — the runs that died land too

**Met. A turn-cap death, a 429 and a timeout each left a real transcript in the store.** The first pass could not show this, because every death in its five hours died before the model wrote anything.

**The window** runs from the deploy (2026-10-01 17:02 PT) to this record (2026-10-17). The deaths were found by the fingerprint table, then each one's stored object was downloaded and read. The operator caused none of them.

```
-- make db-read (13:33 PT)
SELECT ending, job, count(*) FROM agent_run_fingerprint WHERE log_date >= '2026-10-02' GROUP BY ending, job;
```

## Observation 3 — a plan run's kept log is the last model step's, with that step's effort

**Met, on both halves.** The plan job's "Keep the run's working log" step reads `ORDER` (`oocritic oorevise claude claude_retry prea replan replan_retry preb posta postreplan postreplan_retry rollup rollup_retry`). It walks it backwards to the last step whose outcome is not `skipped`. If that step succeeded, it stamps that step's `EFFORT_<id>`. If it failed, it writes `kept model step: <id> (failed — transcript ownership unconfirmed, no effort stamped)`. The `kept model step:` line goes to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which `gh run view --log` does not return, so it was not read as text. **The inputs to the step that writes it were read instead,** from its `env:` group in the run log (`gh run view <id> --log`). Which model step produced the stored transcript was matched by `session_id`: the object's `system`/`init` session id appears in exactly one `claude-code-action` group in the run log.

**A plan run that died in a later model step:** bureau-pipeline `38329761597`, DRE-7066, job 2026-10-12 17:57–18:03 PT.

- The step outcomes were `OUTCOME_oocritic: success` and `OUTCOME_oorevise: failure`, with every later step `skipped`. So the kept step is `oorevise`, the revise step that runs after the critic, and the summary line takes its failed branch.
- The run log holds two `claude-code-action` groups, starting at lines 1010 and 1724. The stored object's session `717f30c4-…` is printed inside the second group, which is `oorevise` (`--max-turns 36`). The object is that later step's transcript, not the critic's. It ends `result` / `error_max_turns` at 37 turns: the revise step ran out of turns.
- **The object carries no `effort` metadata:** `aws s3api head-object` returned `Metadata: {}`. The fingerprint row reads `effort` NULL, `ending` `turn_cap`.

**A healthy plan-route run:** agent-bureau `38314378287` attempt 2, DRE-7072, job 2026-10-12 15:35–15:46 PT.

- The step outcomes were `claude`, `prea`, `replan` and `preb` all `success`, each with `EFFORT_<id>: --effort high`, and every later step `skipped`. So the kept step is `preb`, and the success branch stamps `--effort high`.
- The run log holds four `claude-code-action` groups (lines 1903, 3752, 4652 and 5878). The stored object's session `3d96f82d-…` is in the fourth, `preb`.
- **The object carries `effort: high`**, matching `EFFORT_preb`.

**Read against the card's words:** the card expected the healthy run's stored object to be "the first critic's transcript". On this run the plan was revised once, so the last model step to succeed is the **second** critic (`preb`), and that is the transcript kept. This is what DRE-5350's rule says, since the last step that ran owns the file. A run that the first critic passed outright would keep `prea`. Not every recent plan run was searched for one.

## Observation 4 — planted fake secrets never survive

**Waiting for a sandbox build on agent-bureau-demo with `BUREAU_PLANT_PROBE` set, run 11 PM–3 AM PT. No secret has been planted yet.** On 2026-10-17 the plant still needed one of the two routes the first pass wrote out:

- **Route A** echoes a real credential the agent holds. That must be followed by rotating that credential, which is a live change outside this observation pass.
- **Route B** needs a one-line change to bureau-pipeline's `agent-task.yml` to put a throwaway secret in the agent step's `env:`.

Neither was taken on 10-17. A run that "passed" without one would read exactly like success while testing nothing, which is the trap the first pass names. The procedure in the first pass's observation 3 stands unchanged. **This keeps the scrub's by-value pass unproven.**

**Changed since 10-17:** route B shipped as DRE-7513 (Done, in bureau-pipeline's `stable`): the build agent's shell carries a throwaway `BUREAU_PLANT_PROBE` secret, so the plant needs no real credential and no further pipeline change. What remains is one sandbox build that echoes it, run at night because it is a live run, and then reading the stored object for the value and the scrub's by-value marker.

**What was read instead, and what it does and does not show.** A one-in-twenty sample of every working log since 2026-10-02 was taken: 382 objects, 242,551,392 characters, all valid JSON, downloaded 13:38 PT. It was scanned with the first pass's two nets:

```
redaction markers: by value 0; by shape 17  («redacted-shape:aws-access-key-id» 13, «…:jwt» 2, «…:anthropic-key» 2)
net A (independent patterns): Anthropic key 18, in 2 files
net B (the scrub's own SHAPES, bureau-pipeline@stable scripts/secret_shapes.py): no match
```

- **The by-shape pass now fires on three shapes**, where the first pass saw one.
- **Net B is empty**, so no text the scrub should have caught got past it.
- **Net A's 18 hits are fixtures, not tokens.** They are in `37516061909-1-review` and `37529441327-1-execute` (agent-bureau, 2026-10-06). They were inspected masked: every one is `sk-ant-oat01-` followed by 15–19 characters ending in words like `…secret` or `…EN-bbb`. That is below the scrub's 20-character floor and far shorter than a real token.
- **By-value markers: still zero**, so pass 1 has still never acted.

"No secret found" is not "the scrub works", for the reason the first pass gives.
